title: Eco Sun: a whole township launched at once in Batu Kawan.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #424 | ECO SUN, BATU KAWAN
excerpt: The next 75-acre township from the team behind Eco Horizon, launching its landed homes, an affordable apartment project and shop offices together. Sean likes the certainty a mature Batu Kawan now offers, but notes the empty land and an awkward upstairs bathroom.
takeaways: Shop offices from about RM2.1 million, landed homes at about RM800,000 and apartments under RM500,000, launched together.
Shops in the team's earlier township are fully let at about RM6,000 to RM8,500 a month.
Batu Kawan still feels empty, and the 20 ft homes put the shared bathroom in the middle of the upstairs hall.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Instead of building phase by phase, the developer is launching almost all of Eco Sun's 75 acres at once: 96 individual-title shop offices, a first landed phase of 528 homes, an affordable apartment project called Irama, a public park and a lake. The whole site is already being cleared.

The landed homes are 20 ft wide and face north and south. One main road branches into private cul-de-sacs behind a double-gated guardhouse, so no house faces a junction. Sean toured a corner-unit model in the developer's immersive experience room, which walks buyers through the street and house at near full scale.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: Eco Sun sits beside the Batu Kawan stadium, near Design Village and the developer's earlier Eco Horizon township, with a Chinese primary school under construction next to it, a wet market and food court coming, the BKIP 3 industrial park expanding nearby and the sea beyond. Roads, street lights and drains around the perimeter are already complete, and local roads run three lanes each way under rain trees.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: At Eco Horizon, shop offices let for about RM6,000 to RM8,000 a month and are fully tenanted; in its Borealis precinct, sold at about RM2 to RM2.1 million, rents are about RM6 psf, roughly RM7,500 to RM8,500 a unit. Here 20 of the 96 shop offices were left when Sean filmed, and the developer helps owners find tenants.

standout.title: Every street a cul-de-sac
standout.body: A single main road branches into private roads that end in cul-de-sacs, so only the people living on a road ever drive down it and no house faces a junction. Back lanes and the perimeter are landscaped as part of the same plan.

pros: The developer has delivered since the beginning: from its first leasehold landed strata phase, when Batu Kawan had nothing, it won buyers over to paying maintenance fees for a landed home and built communities and tenant mixes, not just buildings. Sean is himself a buyer of one of their KL projects.

The confidence to launch everything together, shop offices from about RM2.1 million, landed homes at about RM800,000 and Irama at under RM500,000, which takes experience and financial strength and serves very different buyers.
The timing: by handover the school, shops and industrial expansion will all be running, so unlike the early days of Eco Horizon, buyers know what they are getting, the market rents and the returns.
cons: The old debate: many Penangites don't see Batu Kawan as Penang. At this price it is one of the only ways to get a new landed home in the state, but it only makes sense if you are raising a family and your work allows it.
Plenty of empty land: on paper everything is sold and tenanted, yet from the air and on the road Batu Kawan still feels empty, especially next to the island.

Facilities and design: Eco Horizon's clubhouse is pay-per-use and Eco Sun has only common play areas, the lake sits outside the guardhouse to keep maintenance fees down, and a gate on the landed homes surprised him. Upstairs, the 20 ft width puts the shared bathroom in the middle of the family hall, opposite the stairs.

closing: A low-risk way into a new landed home in Penang for families whose work is on the mainland, backed by a developer that has already proven itself here.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this January 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. The developer's team showed Sean the site, its earlier township and an immersive model of the house; prices and rents are as he quoted them. Sean says he has bought one of the developer's projects in KL.
